title.title: Threshold parallel repetition for entangled games
title.subtitle: Claim: winning a $v + \delta$ fraction of $k$ parallel rounds is exponentially unlikely, for any finite game

beats.text: Entangled players play $k$ copies of a game with value $v < 1$ in parallel
Claim: winning a $v + \delta$ fraction of the rounds becomes exponentially unlikely
Constants illustrative; the paper's rate is $\delta^5$, the Lean's $\delta^{13}$

achievement.label: Threshold parallel repetition, entangled games
achievement.context: Before: XOR, free and anchored games; only polynomial decay for general games (Yuen 2016)
achievement.note: The hard all-wins step is credited to prior work, including OpenAI's own

verify.detail: Lean proves it with $\delta^{13}$ in place of the paper's $\delta^5$
verify.ourCheck: We compared the Lean scope with the claim; we did not build it

sources.quote: with delta^13 in place of the paper's delta^5

plain: Two players cheat with shared quantum links; play many rounds at once and big winning streaks become rare

steps: Play many copies of the game at the same time
A known conditioning estimate controls rounds one at a time
So wins concentrate: beating the value is exponentially rare

voice.text: Entangled players play many copies at once: how often do they beat the value?
A known conditioning estimate, applied round by round, makes the number of wins concentrate.
Claimed: exponentially unlikely, for every finite game.
